newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US Eurodollar vols steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US Eurodollar vols steady in quiet trade.

text.p: Trading in Eurodollar futures options at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) ground to a halt in late morning, with the bond market closed for the Veterans Day holiday, dealers said.
CME Eurodollars also close early at 1200 CST/1800 GMT.
"Today is not even a trading day," said a brokerage firm trader on the CME floor. "There's nobody in, we haven't taken any orders, we're just warm bodies here."
Traders said market-makers had taken time decay for today out of option premiums already in Friday's late trade.
Implied volatility for March Eurodollar futures options stood at around 11.8 percent.

One firm was seen buying 1,000 lots of 93.75 puts in short-December contracts -- mid-curve options based on December 1997 futures but expiring in December 1996 -- but that was about the only notable deal, traders said.

Traders expected volatilities to be bid up on Tuesday ahead of Wednesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting and U.S. inflation data later in the week, although few saw any near-term changes in the Federal Reserve's monetary policy.
October U.S. producer price index (PPI) is due out Wednesday and consumer price index (CPI) on Thursday.

Economists polled by Reuters have, on average, forecast a rise of 0.2 percent in the overall October PPI against a 0.2 percent gain a month earlier. They also expected overall CPI to rise 0.3 percent versus 0.2 percent in September.
